cards.claim: Detecting eye blinks is a challenging problem with applications in revealing deep fake manipulation, detecting driver drowsiness, and measuring attention levels.
cards.evidence_quote: Detecting eye blinks is a challenging problem that can be used to solve a number of facial analysis tasks; it can reveal deep fake manipulation, detect driver drowsiness

cards.claim: Most existing approaches rely on face recognition and frame-wise classification, which struggle with short blinks or noisy data.
cards.evidence_quote: Most approaches depend on face recognition and frame-wise eye state classiﬁcation... However, these methods may struggle to handle cases where blinks occur for only a few frames

cards.claim: Feature-based methods use predetermined higher-level features like iris and eye landmark distances to detect blinks.
cards.evidence_quote: (i) feature-based methods use predetermined higher-level features like iris and eye landmark distances

cards.claim: Appearance-based methods utilize low-level eye representations such as RGB texture and learning algorithms to classify eye states.
cards.evidence_quote: (ii) appearance-based methods utilize low-level eye representations (e.g., RGB texture) and then adopt learning algorithms to classify eye states

cards.claim: The authors propose BlinkLinMulT, a fast transformer-based framework that combines low- and high-level feature sequences to detect eye blinks.
cards.evidence_quote: In this work, we propose a fast transformer-based framework for eye blink detection that can effectively combine low- and high-level feature sequences

cards.claim: BlinkLinMulT utilizes a modified multi-modal transformer with linear attention to process multiple inputs including RGB texture, landmarks, and head pose angles.
cards.evidence_quote: We present a modiﬁed multi- modal transformer with linear attention (LinMulT) [21], which considers multiple inputs, such as RGB texture, iris and eye landmarks

cards.claim: The proposed model is the first to use transformer architecture for efficient fusion of input features including head pose angles.
cards.evidence_quote: To our knowledge, this is the ﬁrst work to use transformer architecture and implement an efﬁcient fusion of input features, including head pose angles.

cards.claim: Cross-dataset evaluations demonstrate that a single network trained on a union of datasets improves results compared to training on separate datasets.
cards.evidence_quote: it is found that a single network trained on a union of datasets improves the results obtained on all datasets separately.

cards.claim: The proposed BlinkLinMulT model replaces quadratic attention modules with linear versions to improve training ease while maintaining performance.
cards.evidence_quote: we replaced the quadratic attention modules with linear versions [28], providing similar performance [21] while being easier to train.

cards.claim: Cross-modal transformers translate information between modalities by learning keys and values from one modality and queries from another.
cards.evidence_quote: Cross-modal transformers translate one information source ... to another one ... by learning keys and values of modality β and the queries from the α modality.

cards.claim: The system uses a linear attention mechanism to increase efficiency by reducing computational resources such as time and memory.
cards.evidence_quote: A linear attention mechanism is used within the networks to increase efﬁciency by reducing computational resources, i.e., time and memory.

cards.claim: The final output uses a fully connected layer with sigmoid applied to logits to determine blink presence and frame-wise eye states.
cards.evidence_quote: Finally, we used a fully connected layer on top of the transformers, which is used for two tasks: (i) ... determine whether blinking is present ... (ii) ... determine eye states.

cards.claim: The proposed BlinkLinMulT model uses a backbone CNN to extract deep features from eye patches, which are then processed by a linear multimodal transformer to estimate blinks for each eye independently.
cards.evidence_quote: a backbone CNN extracts deep hidden representations of the RGB eye patches. These sets of features are utilized as inputs to a linear multimodal transformer that estimates blinks for each eye independently.

cards.claim: The final blink presence score is determined by averaging network logits and applying a sigmoid function to the estimations from both left and right eyes.
cards.evidence_quote: The network logits are averaged, and a sigmoid function is applied to make a ﬁnal decision to obtain the ﬁnal blink presence score for the sequence

cards.claim: The system utilizes specific facial landmarks including eye aspect ratio, iris diameter, and eyelid-pupil distance as inputs for blink calculations.
cards.evidence_quote: which are used for EAR, iris diameter, and eyelid–pupil distance calculations.

cards.claim: The blink estimation pipeline is organized into a structured sequence involving feature generation, head pose processing, and the BlinkLinMulT model.
cards.evidence_quote: The components are organized into a pipeline, which can be seen in Figure 2.

cards.claim: The CEW dataset was created by Song et al. using 2423 subjects, with eye patches resized to 64x64 pixels and evaluated via 10-fold cross-validation.
cards.evidence_quote: The Closed Eyes in the Wild (CEW) dataset was created by Song et al. [29]. Close face crops are collected from 2423 subjects... resized to 64 × 64 pixels... employed a 10-fold cross-validation (CV) scheme

cards.claim: The MRL Eye dataset contains 84,898 infrared images from thirty-seven participants captured under various lighting and reflection conditions.
cards.evidence_quote: The MRL Eye dataset [32] was collected from thirty-seven participants... This dataset contains 84,898 infrared images in low and high resolution

cards.claim: For the RT-GENE dataset, eye patches were extracted from RGB images and annotated as RT-BENE, with specific subjects used for testing.
cards.evidence_quote: Eye patches are extracted from the face images and then annotated and published as RT-BENE [8]. ... subjects with IDS 0, 14, 15, and 16 are used as the test set.

cards.claim: The Researcher's Night dataset includes 107 videos with 223,000 frames of people reading or blinking in cluttered backgrounds.
cards.evidence_quote: The authors of the dataset collected 107 videos with 223,000 frames of different people with various head poses and cluttered backgrounds.

cards.claim: The BlinkLinMulT model was trained for 50 epochs using video samples, while CNN backbones required 310 epochs on image datasets.
cards.evidence_quote: The CNN backbones were trained for 310 epochs on the image datasets, whilst BlinkLinMulT was trained for 50 epochs using samples extracted from the video datasets.

cards.claim: ResNet50 achieved the highest F1 score of 0.912 on the unbalanced RT-BENEimg dataset, outperforming other backbones by a considerable margin.
cards.evidence_quote: DenseNet121 performed well with 0.883, but ResNet50 outperformed the other models by a considerable margin with a 0.912 F1 score and 0.946 AP.

cards.claim: Increasing image resolution from 64x64 to 224x224 for ResNet50 resulted in lower performance metrics across all evaluated measures.
cards.evidence_quote: The CNN trained on the 224 × 224 images achieved lower performance metric scores in every case versus its 64 × 64 counterpart

cards.claim: Models trained on the ZJU dataset showed massive performance degradation when evaluated on unseen datasets, with F1 scores dropping by up to 46%.
cards.evidence_quote: the same network can only achieve 0.652 on the CEW and 0.502 on the RT-BENEimg, showing a massive performance degradation, 30%, and 46%, respectively.

cards.claim: Training on the union of multiple datasets improved F1 scores across CEW, ZJU, and RT-BENEimg benchmarks.
cards.evidence_quote: Training on the union of the datasets improved on previous results measured in Section 4.2: the F1 scores changed from 0.995 to 0.997 on CEW, from 0.927 to 0.933 on ZJU, and from 0.883 to 0.913 RT-BENEimg.

cards.claim: The BlinkLinMulT model predicts frame-wise eye state scores to determine blink event positions and presence.
cards.evidence_quote: The proposed BlinkLinMulT predicts frame-wise eye state scores, which are also used for determining the position of the blink event within the sequence, and then the blink presence is determined

cards.claim: A 3.8% performance degradation was observed when not fine-tuning the network with MRL images.
cards.evidence_quote: We observed a 3.8% degradation if we are not ﬁne-tuning the network using the MRL images

cards.claim: Adding the MRL training set to the union of training databases increased the F1 score by 2%.
cards.evidence_quote: and also the F1 score is increased by 2% if the MRL train set is added to the union of the training databases.

cards.claim: Training on a union of diverse datasets improves eye state recognition and blink presence detection performance compared to using single datasets.
cards.evidence_quote: Table 6 shows that the eye state recognition and blink presence detection performance are consistently improved compared to those experiments, where only a single dataset is used for training.

cards.claim: The proposed BlinkLinMulT model generalizes well across public benchmark datasets because it is trained once on the union of all datasets.
cards.evidence_quote: While, in the literature, the proposed models are retrained for each dataset, our network is trained once and performs well on all the public blink benchmark datasets.

cards.claim: The BlinkLinMulT model achieves superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art methods across various datasets and tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: We show that our method generalizes well to different scenarios, and the performance of our network is comparable to or surpasses the performance of state-of-the-art methods

cards.claim: Combining iris/eye landmark features with RGB texture improves performance over using texture alone.
cards.evidence_quote: combining them with the texture further improves the performance on RT-BENEimg compared to texture-only evaluation (0.922 vs. 0.913 F1 scores).

cards.claim: The BlinkLinMulT model achieves a perfect F1 score of 1.0 for blink presence detection on the TalkingFace dataset when using all feature sequences.
cards.evidence_quote: the problematic extreme blinks when the person looks down are detected in TalkingFace, achieving a 1.0 F1 score in the blink presence detection task.

cards.claim: Transformer-based sequence modeling outperforms frame-wise estimations for detecting blinking dynamics.
cards.evidence_quote: In Table 9, the transformer- based sequence modeling shows superiority over frame-wise estimations.

cards.claim: Model performance drops at higher yaw angles due to self-occlusion making prediction harder for the network.
cards.evidence_quote: the performance of the model drops at higher yaw angles compared to the frontal faces

cards.claim: Errors primarily originate from extreme head pose cases where participants are looking down, as eyelids move over a shorter distance.
cards.evidence_quote: Most of the errors originated from this extreme head pose because the eyelids are more visible, they move over a shorter distance

cards.claim: The proposed BlinkLinMulT model utilizes a modified multimodal transformer with linear attention to efficiently fuse RGB texture, iris/eye landmarks, and head pose features for eye blink detection.
cards.evidence_quote: Specifically, we modiﬁed the multimodal transformer with linear attention (LinMulT), which fuses multiple inputs, such as RGB texture, iris and eye landmarks features, and head pose angles.

cards.claim: Cross-dataset evaluations demonstrate that training a single network on a union of datasets improves robustness and results across all individual unseen datasets.
cards.evidence_quote: We performed cross-dataset evaluations to assess the robustness of BlinkLinMulT on unseen samples, demonstrating that a single network trained on a union of datasets improves results across all datasets indi-vidually.

cards.claim: The model achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art models on blink presence detection and eye state recognition tasks using public benchmark databases.
cards.evidence_quote: Our results demonstrate comparable or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models on blink presence detection and eye state recognition tasks, using public benchmark databases.

cards.claim: The study shows that increased eye patch dimensionality of low-resolution patches degrades the performance of current SOTA backbones like CLIP ViT-B/16.
cards.evidence_quote: We showed how increased eye patch dimensionality of low-resolution eye patches degrades the performance of current SOTA backbones, e.g., CLIP ViT-B/16 dependence

cards.claim: The BlinkLinMulT model maintains high accuracy across various yaw angles, with performance slightly decreasing at extreme orientations greater than 25 degrees.
cards.evidence_quote: Extreme yaw and pitch angles, when the participant is looking sideways or down, might cause slightly decreased performance.

cards.claim: The proposed BlinkLinMulT method achieves its highest F1 score of 0.960 on samples with yaw angles less than -25 degrees.
Performance drops significantly for pitch angles greater than 25 degrees, resulting in an F1 score of only 0.744.
The evaluation uses test samples from all five sequence datasets to assess the head pose angle dependence of the proposed model.
cards.evidence_quote: Test samples from all 5 sequence datasets are used for the experiment.
